core_obligations: Reduce to connectedness of the intersection: the component is contained in the intersection of all clopen neighbourhoods, so it suffices to show that intersection is connected (proof lines 2085-2092)
Assume a separation of the intersection into disjoint clopen parts; the parts are closed and hence quasi-compact, so they can be separated by disjoint opens of the space (proof lines 2093-2098)

Finiteness: the complement of the union of those opens is closed and quasi-compact, so by the finite intersection criterion some clopen neighbourhood is contained in the union, which splits into two clopen pieces, contradicting the connectedness of the neighbourhood (proof lines 2099-2108)
proof_roadmap: 令 T 为连通分支、S = ∩_{α} Z_α（过 x 的一切开闭子集之交，闭）；T ⊂ S，只需证 S 连通。
若 S = B ∐ C（在 S 中开闭），则 B、C 在 X 中闭 ⇒ 准紧 ⇒ 可取不交开集 U ⊃ B、V ⊃ C。
X ∖ (U ∪ V) 闭 ⇒ 准紧 ⇒ 由「有限交非空则全交非空」存在 α 使 Z_α ∩ (X ∖ (U ∪ V)) = ∅，即 Z_α ⊂ U ∪ V；于是 Z_α = (Z_α ∩ U) ∐ (Z_α ∩ V) 是两个开闭片之并，与 Z_α 连通矛盾（故 C = ∅）。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that in a quasi-compact Hausdorff space the connected component of a point is the intersection of all clopen subsets containing it (author lemma at source lines 2077-2083, label lemma-connected-component-intersection-compact-Hausdorff). The proof (source lines 2085-2109) reduces to connectedness of that intersection, assumes a separation, separates the two closed pieces by disjoint opens and uses the finite intersection criterion to find a clopen neighbourhood contained in their union, which splits it (proof lines 2085-2108). The separation and the clopen splitting are the substance. H3.
